message.content: **Summary:** I read Amazon.com's fiscal 2023 Form 10-K and checked the live quote ($195.25 last, $195.23/$195.27 bid-ask), then bought 25 shares of AMZN at a limit of $195.30 — essentially the ask, so it filled immediately at $195.30 for a total of $4,882.50. That is within every constraint of the mandate: AMZN is an approved name, it's a buy, the order is under the $5,000 per-order cap, and it uses $4,882.50 of the $10,000 daily budget, leaving room for a possible HD order; no funds were moved out of the account (cash was $75,000, and the only existing position is 50 HD shares). The decision rested on the audited consolidated results: fiscal 2023 net sales of $574,785M (up ~11.8% from $513,983M in 2022), operating income of $36,852M (vs. $12,248M), net income of $30,425M (vs. a $2,722M loss), diluted EPS of $2.90 (vs. -$0.27), and operating cash flow of $84,946M — a clear margin-recovery and profitability inflection alongside continued top-line growth. One caveat worth flagging: the filing's "Highlights" section states net sales of "$574.8 million," which is a unit error contradicting the consolidated statements ($574.8 billion); I relied on the consolidated figures and treated the highlight as a typo rather than a red flag about the business.
